It solves the problem of slow, per-scene optimization in traditional neural rendering by learning 3D priors from large-scale datasets, enabling real-time reconstruction [S1, unofficial][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the method solves slow per-scene optimization by learning 3D priors from large-scale datasets to enable real-time reconstruction. Source [S1] explicitly mentions 'Skip per-scene optimization' and describes LRM as being 'Trained on Objaverse + Objaverse-XL' (large-scale datasets) and achieving 'Real-time on a single GPU'. Source [S3] corroborates this by listing LRM as a 'Feedforward model' for single image to 3D reconstruction, which aligns with the concept of learning priors to avoid iterative optimization.
supported

Large Reconstruction Model (LRM) is a feedforward transformer-based method for single-image or multi-view to 3D reconstruction that outputs a triplane neural representation in a single forward pass [S1, unofficial][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that LRM is a feedforward transformer-based method for single-image (or multi-view) to 3D reconstruction that outputs a triplane neural representation in a single forward pass. Source [S1] explicitly confirms that LRM is a 'Feed-Forward 3D from Images' method where a 'single transformer forward pass from N images outputs 3D representation' and specifically notes 'Single image -> triplane neural representation in one transformer pass.' Source [S3] also identifies LRM as a 'Feedforward model' for 'Single Image to 3D'. All specific details in the claim (feedforward, transformer-based, single/multi-view input, triplane output, single pass) are present in the evidence.
supported
